ennedi-plateau.name: Ennedi Plateau
ennedi-plateau.summary: Sandstone plateau in northeast Chad, part of the Sahara, occupied by hunter-gatherers and later pastoralists from around 5,000 BC, known for ancient rock art.

wadi-howar.name: Wadi Howar
wadi-howar.summary: A wadi (dry riverbed) running through Sudan and Chad, also known as the Yellow Nile.

tibesti-mountains.name: Tibesti Mountains
tibesti-mountains.summary: A mountain range in the central Sahara, mostly in northern Chad, home to the Toubou people and site of the highest peaks in Chad and Libya.

african-humid-period.name: African humid period
african-humid-period.summary: A wetter climate phase in Africa during the late Pleistocene and Holocene, when the Sahara was covered in grasses, trees and lakes, lasting roughly from 14,600 to about 5,000 years ago.

ishango-bone.name: Ishango bone
ishango-bone.summary: Roughly 10-centimetre Upper Paleolithic bone tool from Ishango, perhaps a counting device or lunar calendar. It has been called "the oldest mathematical tool of humankind", though older engraved bones exist.

kalambo-falls.name: Kalambo Falls
kalambo-falls.summary: 235-metre waterfall on the Zambia–Tanzania border, one of Africa's tallest. Its site was occupied for over 447,000 years, and wooden structures about 476,000 years old were found there in 2023.

magosian.name: Magosian
magosian.summary: Archaeological industry of southern and eastern Africa dated to between 10,000 and 6,000 BC, distinguished by its use of microliths and small blades.

ishango.name: Ishango
ishango.summary: Lakeshore fishing village in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, near one of the sources of the Nile. It is known for its biodiversity and archaeological finds showing early human occupation.

san-peoples.name: San people
san-peoples.summary: Indigenous hunter-gatherer peoples of southern Africa and among the oldest surviving cultures in the region, with ancestry possibly diverging from other humans 100,000 to 200,000 years ago.

cape-agulhas.name: Cape Agulhas
cape-agulhas.summary: The southernmost point of South Africa and the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans, long known to sailors as a hazard on the clipper route.

janette-deacon.name: Janette Deacon
janette-deacon.summary: South African archaeologist (born 1939) specializing in heritage management and rock art conservation, who studied changes in stone tools over 20,000 years and located rock engravings tied to 19th-century /Xam informants.

african-pygmies.name: African Pygmies
african-pygmies.summary: Central African ethnic groups, including the Mbenga, Mbuti and Twa, traditionally living by foraging and hunting in the Congo Basin, descended from the region's earliest Middle Stone Age inhabitants.

central-sudanic-languages.name: Central Sudanic languages
central-sudanic-languages.summary: A family of about sixty languages proposed as part of Nilo-Saharan, spoken across Central Africa, including by pygmy peoples such as the Efé and Asoa.

ubangian-languages.name: Ubangian languages
ubangian-languages.summary: A diverse group of about seventy languages spoken by 2 to 3 million people, centered on the Central African Republic (where Sango is an official language) and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

wilton-culture.name: Wilton culture
wilton-culture.summary: Archaeologists' term for sites and cultures sharing similar stone-tool technology dating from about 8,000 to 4,000 years ago, treated as a technocomplex.
